title: Residents protest housing costs and mass tourism in Barcelona
seoTitle: Barcelona protest over housing and tourism

tea.why: Residents are protesting skyrocketing housing costs, short-term vacation rentals, and mass tourism.
tea.want: Demonstrators are demanding solutions to the housing affordability crisis and calling for a general strike.
tea.changed: Oct 14: Fox News reported that hundreds of thousands of residents flooded streets in Barcelona, Madrid, and other cities.

summary: Residents in Barcelona and multiple other Spanish cities have engaged in mass demonstrations following the eviction and subsequent death of an 87-year-old pensioner, María del Carmen Abascal. The protesters are voicing deep frustration over soaring housing costs, short-term vacation rentals, and mass tourism, which they argue have priced locals out of the housing market. Authorities including Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez have publicly addressed the housing pressures, while federal and local governments attempt to implement changes such as tourism taxes and restrictions. Meanwhile, political groups and labor bureaucracies like the CCOO and UGT have called for a nationwide protest strike, while groups such as the Corriente Revolucionaria de Trabajadores (CRT) intervene in the unfolding unrest.
response: According to the sources, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni have publicly addressed the housing and tourism issues, and the government has attempted to implement changes including visitor taxes.

updates.text: Following the death of an 87-year-old pensioner after a forced eviction, thousands demonstrated in multiple cities.
Fox News reported that hundreds of thousands of residents flooded the streets in Barcelona, Madrid, and other cities.
